title: Mega Backdoor Roth via business 401(k)
summary: If your 401(k) plan allows after-tax contributions plus in-plan Roth conversions, fill the after-tax space.
detailsHtml:
Setting up Mega Backdoor Roth capability in your own business 401(k) is one of the highest-leverage plan-design decisions you can make. Adds significant cost (custom plan document, more administration), but for high-income owners typically pays for itself in 1–2 years of conversions.

Configure automatic in-plan Roth conversion per IRS Notice 2014-54. Earnings on after-tax contributions are ordinary-income taxable at conversion. When you're designing the plan document for the first time, spec same-payroll automatic in-plan Roth conversion as the default — quarterly or annual manual conversion leaks earnings to ordinary rates. The plan-document line item costs nothing extra; getting it wrong costs every participant 3–4 figures per year in unnecessary tax for the full duration the plan operates.
